messages:
raja: Heads-up — small but persistent p95 ridge (~12-25ms) for short LLM RPCs from a handful of hosts in rack r81 since ~05:20 UTC. Not a batch job. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/d/egress/r81

ops-bot: [Alert] egress-p95-elevated on rack r81 (05:22 UTC). Runbook: https://confluence.internal/runbooks/egress-noise

claire: Any obvious tenant spike? Can you run the attribution to top sender pid/cgroup?

raja: Ran quick snapshot. Top transmitter on node-a2 is tenant-411-metrics (pid 8821). Host dump below:
```
r81-node-a2:
  tx_queue_len: 38
  p95_rtt_ms: 21.4
  irq_pps: 97k
  softirq_skew: cpu1
  top_sender: tenant-411-metrics-sidecar:9200 (pid 8821)
```

sophie: This looks like small-packet telemetry causing NIC coalesce thrash + softirq concentration. Low friction mitigation order: 1) spread IRQ affinity, 2) apply per-tenant egress policing (tc/classify by cgroup), 3) nudge exporter to add jitter in polling, 4) micro-proxy pool or micro-slice if it recurs, 5) full dedicated slice as last resort.

jules: Finance, can you give a quick delta for micro-proxy vs dedicated slice so Support knows what to propose to customers? Micro-proxy = prewarmed small L7 pool; dedicated slice = GPU reservation.

eng-finance: Quick ballpark: micro-proxy pool (4 reserved proxy workers pinned) ≈ 1.2x marginal cost at peak vs shared. Tiny dedicated GPU slice (single-GPU reserved + replica) ≈ 2.5x marginal. Micro-proxy isolates L7 and proxy contention; it won't fully solve NIC-level contention from token streams.

claire: For immediate relief I'll apply irq-affinity spread to r81-node-a[1-3] and watch 10m. If p95 > 6ms after that we'll apply a tc throttle on the tenant cgroup as a canary.

ops-bot: Action queued: apply-irq-affinity-spread -> r81-node-a[1-3] (05:34 UTC)

raja: IRQ spread applied. After 5m p95 improved from 21.4ms -> 7.9ms, tx_queue_len -> 18. Improvement but above baseline (~3ms).

claire: Applying per-tenant soft-throttle (canary) on node-a2: 120mbit with 12ms burst via tc classifying cgroup. Command snippet:
```
# classify tenant cgroup + shape
tc qdisc add dev eth0 root handle 1: htb default 30
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1: classid 1:10 htb rate 120mbit burst 12kb
tc filter add dev eth0 protocol ip parent 1:0 prio 1 handle 100 cgroup
```

ops-bot: Per-tenant egress-policing applied for tenant-411 on r81-node-a2 (05:42 UTC).

raja: After policing p95 -> 3.4ms on the canary host. Rolling watch for 20m. Looks like policing + irq spread is effective.

claire: Follow-ups: (1) add auto-attribution to egress alerts so future p95 alerts include top-cgroup/pid and suggest the standard play; (2) add exporter polling-jitter default to telemetry helm chart; (3) draft a micro-proxy runbook and cost appendix. I'll file the tickets.

jules: Please include tangible cost numbers and operational caveats in the ticket so support's escalation template can recommend micro-proxy vs dedicated slice correctly. I'll attach a short appendix.

eng-finance: Adding note: micro-proxy isolates L7 but not NIC if tenant turns into heavy streaming; if that happens dedicated slice is appropriate. Also note micro-proxy setup time is short (minutes) vs dedicated GPU carveout (tens of minutes to hours depending on capacity).

claire: Ticket filed: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INFRA-9999 7 - auto-attr probe, soft-quarantine playbook, telemetry jitter, and micro-proxy cost appendix. I pasted the diagnostic traces + tcpdumps.

raja: For the runbook I'd like the short play explicitly: 1) apply IRQ-affinity spread -> 5m observe, 2) apply per-tenant policing canary -> 10m observe, 3) if still >8ms or customer-impacting escalate to micro-proxy (include cost) -> consider dedicated slice only as last resort.

ops-bot: Runbook updated by claire (05:58 UTC).

claire: Leaving monitors on for 1h. If we see recurrence we can automate the detection -> soft-quarantine path (auto throttling) but want human-in-loop for first few incidents. :eyes:
